title: Cheese Arepas
description: Corn cakes made from precooked masarepa, griddled until they blister and split open with steam. Four ingredients, and the dough tells you when it is right.
notes: Masarepa is not the same as masa harina and not the same as cornmeal — neither substitute works.

steps.text: Stir the salt into the warm water, then rain in the masarepa, mixing with your hand.
steps.tip: Flour into water, not the other way round — it hydrates evenly and you get no dry pockets.

steps.text: Knead in the queso fresco and let the dough rest so the corn finishes absorbing.
steps.tip: The dough should feel like soft clay. If it cracks at the edge when you flatten it, wet your hands and knead again.

steps.text: Shape into eight discs about a centimetre thick, smoothing the edges between wet palms.
Griddle in butter over a medium heat until a crust forms and they sound hollow, turning once.
steps.tip: A finished arepa puffs slightly and hisses. Do not press it down.
